_comment: Canonical mutate scope for the SHARED-crypto half of the mutation gate (ADR 0045), split out of web/stryker.mutate.json when this package was extracted (cr-admin-web-extraction, ADR 0065). Read by both packages/crypto/stryker.config.mjs (the mutator) and scripts/mutation_meta_check.py (the guard that asserts something was in fact mutated) — two languages, neither able to parse the other's config, so a restated scope would drift the mutator and its guard apart. Paths are package-relative (Stryker's cwd = packages/crypto/). WHY THE SPLIT IS STRUCTURAL, not a filing preference: Stryker's test runner is the project's own vitest, and a project's vitest does not collect a sibling package's suites — so leaving these two entries in web/'s manifest would have mutated files no web test covers and reported a green run over nothing, the precise failure scripts/mutation_meta_check.py exists to catch. The gate has to live where the tests that kill its mutants live. WHAT IS IN, unchanged from the measurements that put it there: v1.ts (97.76% → 100%, the KAT-pinned primitive tier, the one file every other crypto claim rests on) and accountBirth.ts (cr-0177, was 77% with no test → 100% via a seeded-RNG + fixed-identity byte-KAT whose expected wraps use HARDCODED AAD literals, so a mutated source context disagrees; its three Argon KEKs are MOCKED because real Argon is ~2.6 s per buildAccount and Stryker pays that per mutant — KEK byte-correctness is v1.conformance's job). WHAT IS OUT, measured not skipped: the argon workers — argon.worker.ts 0.00% (21/21 NoCoverage, no test instantiates the Worker) and argonWorker.ts 19.67% (worker-vs-fallback PATH survivors: the tests pin the crypto RESULT, byte-identical either way). Both are execution placement, not crypto; scoring them together reports the misleading number ADR 0045 §3 exists to prevent. base64.ts is out for the same reason it was never in: it is transport encoding with a round-trip test, not crypto logic.
